section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of Elul not only grants power but also awakens the desire to greet the King, as understood from the parable of the king in the field.
section.t: And one may add,
that this matter—that the revelation of Elul is not only a granting of power but also an awakening—
is also understood from the general concept of the king in the field,
for when the king is in the field, there is additionally that then each person has permission and ability to greet the king,
the knowledge of the people that the king is in the field,
in that same place where they are,
awakens within them the desire to greet the king.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the people's desire to greet the king stems from their very essence, and the king's presence in the field reveals this latent desire.
section.t: And one may explain this,
that the desire of the people to greet the king is from the very essence of their existence.
For since the king is the heart of all the people,
therefore their connection to the king is in their very essence,
but nevertheless,
when the king and the people are in a distant place,
it is possible that their connection to the king,
and
(consequently also)
their desire to greet him, will be in concealment,
and by the king being in the field,
in that same place where they are,
the desire is revealed.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the awakening to teshuvah in Elul reveals the inner desire of Israel through the revelation of the Name E-l, which is the source of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy and the essence of the Ein Sof light within each Jew.
section.t: And likewise in the analogy,

that the awakening to teshuvah that comes through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy in Elul is that through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, the inner desire of Israel is revealed
[and as is also understood from what is explained later in the maamar
(after the parable of the king in the field),
that the Name E-l is the beginning of all the Thirteen Attributes and their source and their totality.
And the concept of the Name E-l is the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, itself,
as it is written,
"E-l, Hashem, and He illuminated for us,"
for light is like the essence
[and as explained in many places
the difference between light and influence,
that influence is when the influencer contracts himself according to the capacity of the recipient,
and light is of the same kind as the luminary].
And in each one of Israel, this revelation shines,
and moreover, the revelation of the Name E-l in each one of Israel is the prince and ruler within him,
for "Israel" is the letters of "Yud"
"Sar E-l" (prince of G-d).
And this is that the self-nullification to G-dliness in each one of Israel is a self-nullification that transcends reason and intellect,
for in Israel there is a revelation of the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, itself, which is above the chain of descent.
And through the revelation of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy
(in Elul)
whose beginning, source, and totality is E-l,
the aspect of E-l in each one of Israel is awakened and revealed].
And this is that the service of Elul is "I am for my Beloved,"
even though the awakening is through the revelation from above,
for the revelation from above is only a cause through which the inner desire of the person is revealed.
